Title:
In Silico Closed-Loop Metabolic Gating of Glycolytic-to-Oxidative Transition in Ex Vivo CAR-T Perfusion Bioreactors Guided by Structural Bioinformatics and Optical Redox Observability

Authors:
Wayne A. Satz

Affiliation (for profile / author verification):
Department of Emergency Medicine, Lewis Katz School of Medicine at Temple University, Philadelphia, PA 19140, USA (satzwa@temple.edu)

Abstract (1907 / 1920 characters):
Durable chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell responses correlate with infusing stem-like memory cells ($\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{SCM}}$) with high spare respiratory capacity (SRC), yet 168-hour ex vivo perfusion in high glucose and IL-2 drives Warburg glycolysis, mitochondrial depolarization ($h$), and $\mathrm{TOX}^+$ exhaustion. We present an in silico study combining structural bioinformatics, eight-state ODE modeling, discrete-adjoint optimal control, optical observability, and C99 firmware to design falsifiable metabolic gating protocols before wet-lab testing. Crystal structures confirm druggable pockets on PDK1 (PDB: 2Q8G; Ser75 H-bond, 2.50 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$) and SIRT1 (PDB: 4ZZJ; Glu230 hinge, 3.47 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$), whereas AlphaFold v6 models of FOXO1 (pLDDT 50.96) and PGC-1$\alpha$ (pLDDT 52.74) place regulatory modification sites in disordered regions. Extending Paper I, our two-stage Bioreactor-BCR policy separates mitophagy-assisted blastogenesis ($u_1$) from PDH reactivation and $\mathrm{NAD}^+$/SIRT1 consolidation ($u_2$), yielding $62.80\times$ expansion, $73.20\%$ $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{SCM}}$, $\mathrm{SRC} = 4.87\times$, and $h(168\,\mathrm{h}) = 6.73\%$ along the 200-variable Pontryagin Pareto frontier (gradient error $2.04 \times 10^{-10}$). Across $N = 1{,}000$ simulated oncology donors under kinetic dispersion and $\pm 6\%$ OD bias, 4-channel sensing fails ($40.5\%$ pass rate), whereas cell-density-invariant optical redox ratio (ORR) restores observability ($\hat{h}$ RMSE $2.08\%$), lifting 168-hour pass rates from $54.1\%$ (68 h timer) to $58.7\%$ ($p = 8.04 \times 10^{-4}$), retaining $59.4\%$ under $100\%$ Lac:Pyr biofouling ($p = 5.22 \times 10^{-129}$), and reaching $74.0\%$ with adaptive harvest (168-240 h). FPU-free C99 firmware (2,704 B SRAM) achieves $0.0216\%$ Huber-EKF parity and rescues acidosis ($\min\mathrm{pH}\ 6.14 \to 6.91$).

Comments:
20 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. MitoRestorer Series (PAPER2); strictly computational/in silico study with full open-source MIASE simulation and C99 firmware reproducibility at https://github.com/deesatzed/mitorestorer
